mechanism_narrative: Sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC from -17.4% to -8.9% over four weeks indicates recovery momentum. This positive trajectory will continue over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the current baseline deficit.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 3 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -22.7% to -6.6% over four weeks, signaling return-to-office behavior. This workplace recovery directly enables retail-recreation visits during commute windows and lunch periods, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 16.1 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -15% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility exhibits high volatility (40.3% to 12.7% to 50.3%) indicating weather-driven or seasonal outdoor activity shifts. When PARKS exceeds 40%, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 50.3% in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite PARKS remaining above 40%, or PARKS falls below 30% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen from 5.6% to 12.4% to 9.9%, indicating sustained essential-goods purchasing. High grocery mobility correlates with household activity clustering; households making grocery trips also make retail-recreation trips in the same outing, producing positive interaction effect on RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 9% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not co-move positively with GROCERY_PHARM in at least 3 of 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed (-13.4% at t-0w), indicating continued avoidance of public transportation. Persistent transit suppression limits foot traffic to retail corridors dependent on transit access, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery to car-dependent locations only, producing net negative effect over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -12% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -13.4% in t-0w, consistently negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -5% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite sustained transit depression.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 4.4% to 0.7% over four weeks, indicating reduced home-based activity and increased time spent outside residential areas. This outbound shift from home, combined with recovering WORKPLACES, drives RETAIL_REC upward as people spend more time in commercial districts over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 2% while WORKPLACES rises above -10%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 3% in any week, or WORKPLACES falls below -15%, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT suppression (-13.4%) combined with WORKPLACES recovery (-6.6%) indicates a regime shift toward car-dependent commuting and activity patterns. This modal shift favors suburban and car-accessible retail over transit-dependent urban retail, producing net negative effect on aggregate RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -12% AND WORKPLACES above -10% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES divergence at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -8% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points, or WORKPLACES falls below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility at 50.3% in t-0w signals strong seasonal outdoor preference (late spring). When PARKS exceeds 45% and RESIDENTIAL falls below 2%, outdoor recreation fully substitutes for indoor retail-recreation, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks until seasonal conditions shift.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 45% AND RESIDENTIAL below 2% in same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 50.3% and RESIDENTIAL at 0.7% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, or PARKS falls below 35%, or RESIDENTIAL rises above 3% in any week.
